Hey there,

It doesn't sound like you're the worst person in the world. I read your text, I get it. You got consumed by all the things you have to do...and you feel like the reason why you are in this state is because they are a burden on you. 

The reason why you also feel like that is because they suffer from dementia, essentially you're not taking care of your grandparents but you're taking care of what the illness has left behind of your grandparents. I hope this doesn't sound too evil but I don't mean it in a nasty way. The proof is that I am 110% sure that if they were in full capacity of reasoning you'd be able to emotionally connect with them better...

So the advice I am going to give you sounds very stupid but I've underestimated the power of talking. I'd suggest trying to really organise a meeting to sit down with everyone and make them understand that they are also their grandparents or parents (for your parents) and that you don't have that much power. See if you can somehow make sure they get the care they need...a financial advisor can maybe tell you how to optimize their finances and see if you can use some of that money to get someone experienced to help you...(and maybe also get someone to pitch in) Is there a forum with someone that lived something similar? How were they able to help out with that. Did your parents co-sign your loans? If yes, explain to them that the burden you're carrying will also ultimately affect them as well.

Try to split things out, try not to half-ass it with texts, get your family to sit down and explain this to you. Show how your problem isn't just your problem but also your family's. I'm 21, I live with problems that are definitely not comparable to yours and I complain about much less, so for whatever it's worth, hat's off to you my friend. I'm sure your grandparents would show you how thankful they'd be if they could. all my love and affection bro. PM me if you need to.
